text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English inventor and industrialist, SIR RICHARD ARKWRIGHT, was born in 1732. He invented mechanised spinning processes such as the spinning frame powered by water.
Russian Tsar ALEXANDER 1, who defeated NAPOLEON's invasion of Russia in 1812, was born in 1777.
American founder of the Mormons JOSEPH SMITH was born in 1805.

Danish/Australian novelist (whose name is more familiar now because of a certain Queensland politician) MARIE BJELKE-PETERSEN was born in 1874. She wrote "The Mysterious Stranger" and "The Captive Singer". Her books were a mix of romance and religion, with the hero and heroine in one of her books singing "Nearer My God To Thee" at their wedding.
British stage and screen actor MAURICE DENHAM, whose films included "Sunday Bloody Sunday", "Our Man in Havana" and "Julia", was born in 1909.
German statesman HELMUT SCHMIDT, who was the chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany, was born in 1922.
United States guitarist with 'Jefferson Airplane' amd 'Hot Tuna' JORMA KAUKONEN was born in 1940.

American singer/songwriter TIM HARDIN was born in 1941. He never had hits with his own compositions, but they became big hits for other artists. The 'Four Tops', BOBBY DARIN and JOHNNY CASH were successful with "If I Were A Carpenter" and 'PETER, PAUL and MARY' and ROD STEWART scored with "Reason To Believe". TIM died in 1980.
Lead guitarist with 'Iron Maiden' DAVE MURRAY was born in 1958.
** EVENTS **
1888 : Dutch artist VINCENT VAN GOGH cut off his earlobe.

According to fellow painter and friend PAUL GAUGUIN, VAN GOGH and he had quarrelled and in a fit of remorse VAN GOGH took to his ear with a razor. The incident took place in the South of France at Arles, where the artists had been painting. VAN GOGH was placed in the St Remy asylum for his "own safety".
1922 : The world's first regular radio broadcasts for

entertainment were transmitted by the British Broadcasting Corporation. The British Post office had issued licences for members of the public to operate a receiving wireless. The new form of entertainment proved very popular.
1948 : A number of high-ranking Japanese war criminals

were executed. One of the most infamous was General TOJO who had earlier attempted suicide. TOJO tried to cheat the executioner by taking the honourable Japanese course of committing hara kiri. TOJO was Japanese PM from 1941 to 1944 and he was the chief instigator of the attack on Pearl Harbour.
1953 : The Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh started their
Australasian tour in Auckland. The Royal Yacht "Gothic" was met by thousands of well-wishers, in small craft and on the wharves.
1960 : In Fremantle a big crowd greeted the arrival of
the "Oriana", the largest passenger ship to visit Australia.
1969 : One of Australia's longest running television

shows came to an end. "In Melbourne Tonight" and its host GRAHAM KENNEDY ran for 22 years. KENNEDY, who became known as the "King of Melbourne's small screens", was only 23 when he hosted his first program. The end of the program didn't mark the end of his televison career and he has made several return appearances.
1973 : The Shah of Iran doubled oil prices.
1985 : In South Africa, six whites died in a bomb blast
in Durban.
1990 : In a Yugoslavian referendum, the republic of
Slovenia voted in favour of becoming an independent state.
1994 : Former West Australian and English test cricketer
TONY LOCK faced the prospect of a possible re-trial, after a Perth District Court jury was unable to reach a verdict on four sex charges against him.
